page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at 2.6 GHz, with no simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptography.

The instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage. It delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. In benchmark testing, the c7gn.xlarge demonstrates average performance in single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside average memory bandwidth speeds, reaching 386.35 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 107.79 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads.

Performance tradeoffs are visible in specialized workloads. While the instance achieves average scores in software compilation, text processing, and database operations, it exhibits weak performance in ray tracing, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and LLM inference tasks. Passmark testing reveals poor performance in CPU encryption tests. Qualitatively, the arm64 architecture and dedicated core allocation provide a resource-dense, cost-efficient profile for network-optimized compute workloads, making it suitable for static web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose utility computing.
description: The Amazon Web Services c7gn.xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized instance powered by a 2.6 GHz AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs with no hyperthreading, paired with 8.0 GB of memory. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance lacks local storage and GPUs, instead utilizing network-attached storage and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Benchmark results indicate average performance in single-core and multi-core processing, software compilation, and static web serving, though it shows weaker results in cryptographic operations and LLM inference. This hardware profile offers a cost-efficient option for network-heavy, compute-focused workloads such as web serving, software compilation, and database operations that benefit from dedicated physical cores without requiring local storage.
